pinev: Five Mile Hill crest, named in the 1900 Tribune; Baty's 90-ft shaft was sunk from the crest. Crest is the highest point of the dune mass south of the harbour on 2016 Michigan 1 m lidar (237.7 m).
'Just back of the summit' (Grand Rapids Herald 1900), i.e. the landward (east) side of the crest, within the 250 m ring.

Five Mile Hill named as the dune on the state park's east boundary (WPA 1941); name still in use 1934. On lidar the mass has two knobs: 226 m at 43.0561,-86.2413 right above the park and the 237.7 m summit 320 m east, joined by a saddle near 205 m; the 400 m ring covers both.

The Grand Haven city water storage tanks stood on Five Mile Hill (Muskegon Chronicle 1932). On 2016 lidar a round levelled pad about 32 m across sits on the summit at 232 m (43.0564,-86.2371) with a second small pad just S and an access road winding up: the tank site. Pin moved onto it (about 55 m from the old crest pin); the 400 m ring is kept so the W knob stays inside.

tw-mi-grand-haven-light-house-hill-convi.st: A Tribune item of 18 Apr 1900 names Baty's partner as J. R. Robinson, also of Pueblo. By 1932 the city's water storage tanks stood on Five Mile Hill. No later find was reported.
src: Grand Haven Tribune, 31 Dec 1900, p. 3, year review (Newspapers.com 1133973128)
Muskegon Chronicle, 17 Feb 1932, p. 14 (Newspapers.com 1174042281): city water storage tanks on Five Mile Hill

set.v: Gold coins (English sovereigns, per a July 1915 follow-up) in a pot or strong box; estimates from about $300 (wrecking company) to $2,000; a rumoured $19,000 second pot proved unfounded

tw-wi-milwaukee-scholl-homestead-pot-191.st: A Journal follow-up of 8 Jul 1915 ('Found Riches Make Unto Themselves Wings') says the find was a strong box near the base of a wall at 142 Sixth St, holding English sovereigns; the pick-man got $120 and guessed $1,500, while the company held $80 and thought there was no more than $300 in all. No Scholl descendant claimed it, and there was no second pot, no diagram and no later find: the $19,000 story was unfounded.
tw-wi-milwaukee-scholl-homestead-pot-191.t: The July 1915 follow-up found no second pot.
src: Milwaukee Journal, 8 Jul 1915, p. 3, 'Found Riches Make Unto Themselves Wings' (Newspapers.com 1299473854)
